title: Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel Land — Elongated Fastener Hole Repair

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Repair of elongated fastener holes in the fixed leading edge access panel land, by oversize anchor nut, by bushed insert or by a local land doubler depending on how many holes in one land are affected.

sections.purpose: This repair restores elongated or pulled fastener holes in the fixed leading edge access panel land, so that the panel can be refitted without a structural replacement.
sections.damage_assessment: Count the affected holes in each land before choosing a scheme; the count, not the size of any one hole, decides which of the three routes applies. Measure each hole in two planes ninety degrees apart and take the larger reading. Where an anchor nut has been turning, the hole will look acceptable and the anchor nut will be the failed item: check every anchor nut by hand before measuring. Where the panel has been opened more than the count in the maintenance record suggests, expect the whole forward row rather than a few holes, and consider whether the modification with the reduced pitch and bonded strip is the better answer.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the panel using the applicable maintenance task and record the hole condition on the panel map. 2. Count the affected holes in each land. 3. Where one or two holes in a land are affected, ream to the next oversize with the guide bush and install an oversize anchor nut. 4. Where three to five holes are affected, ream and install a bushed insert bonded into the land, and re-drill the insert to the original fastener size. 5. Where more than five holes in one land are affected, install the local land doubler from the repair drawing using the cleat D5720111577697 and the splice plate D5720110130580 as backing. 6. Do an eddy current inspection of every reamed hole before anything is installed. 7. De-burr and clean each hole and remove all swarf from behind the land. 8. Where the doubler route is used, drill the doubler pattern with the jig and install the fasteners wet. 9. Fit the bracket kit D5720111574269 where the drawing calls for the inboard support. 10. Restore the protective scheme in the repaired area. 11. Refit the panel and torque to the value in the maintenance task. 12. Do the water ingress flood test and confirm a dry rib flange.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of every reamed hole at the time of repair and record it against the panel map position. Where the land doubler is fitted, repeat the eddy current inspection of the doubler perimeter row every eight thousand flight cycles. At every panel removal thereafter, record the hole condition on the panel map; the value of this repair is in the trend, and a land that needs a second repair is telling you the panel is being opened more often than the design assumed.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Hole elongation up to 1.5 mm beyond nominal on the larger axis, up to five holes per land for the insert route, and up to eight holes per land for the doubler route. Beyond eight the land is replaced.

materials.description: CLEAT, FIXED LEADING EDGE STRUCTURE, SUB-ASSY
SPLICE PLATE, FIXED LEADING EDGE STRUCTURE

type_data.fastener_pattern: Doubler route: single row at 25 mm pitch with 12 mm edge distance; insert route retains the original pattern
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The insert route carries no life limit. The land doubler is life-limited to 30 000 flight cycles with a repeat eddy current inspection of the perimeter row every 8 000 flight cycles.

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Repair of elongated fastener holes in the fixed leading edge access panel land, by oversize anchor nut, by bushed insert or by a local land doubler, with the constraint each route places on a later change of fastener pitch.

sections.purpose: This repair restores elongated or pulled fastener holes in the fixed leading edge access panel land, so that the panel can be refitted without a structural replacement.
sections.damage_assessment: Count the affected holes in each land before choosing a scheme; the count, not the size of any one hole, decides which of the three routes applies. Measure each hole in two planes ninety degrees apart and take the larger reading. Where an anchor nut has been turning, the hole will look acceptable and the anchor nut will be the failed item: check every anchor nut by hand before measuring. Where the panel has been opened more than the count in the maintenance record suggests, expect the whole forward row rather than a few holes, and consider whether the modification with the reduced pitch and bonded strip is the better answer. That choice is one way only. The land doubler occupies exactly the material the sixty millimetre pitch drills into, so a land that carries a doubler cannot afterwards be taken to the reduced pitch without the doubler coming off, and removing a bonded doubler from a land normally ends in a panel change. Where the modification is already planned for the aircraft, use the insert route up to five holes and refer the sixth to the design office rather than fitting the doubler.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the panel using the applicable maintenance task and record the hole condition on the panel map. 2. Count the affected holes in each land. 3. Where one or two holes in a land are affected, ream to the next oversize with the guide bush and install an oversize anchor nut. 4. Where three to five holes are affected, ream and install a bushed insert bonded into the land, and re-drill the insert to the original fastener size. 5. Where more than five holes in one land are affected, install the local land doubler from the repair drawing using the cleat D5720111577697 and the splice plate D5720110130580 as backing. 6. Do an eddy current inspection of every reamed hole before anything is installed. 7. De-burr and clean each hole and remove all swarf from behind the land. 8. Where the doubler route is used, drill the doubler pattern with the jig and install the fasteners wet. 9. Fit the bracket kit D5720111574269 where the drawing calls for the inboard support. 10. Restore the protective scheme in the repaired area. 11. Refit the panel and torque to the value in the maintenance task. 12. Do the water ingress flood test and confirm a dry rib flange.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do an eddy current inspection of every reamed hole at the time of repair and record it against the panel map position. Where the land doubler is fitted, mark the land on the panel map as doubler-repaired and repeat the eddy current inspection of the doubler perimeter row every eight thousand flight cycles. At every panel removal thereafter, record the hole condition on the panel map; the value of this repair is in the trend, and a land that needs a second repair is telling you the panel is being opened more often than the design assumed. Before a visit that includes the reduced pitch modification, extract every doubler-repaired land from the panel map and hand the list to the planner with the kit order: those lands are either left at the original pitch as a mixed-standard land or the panel is replaced, and neither decision can sensibly be taken with the wing open.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Hole elongation up to 1.5 mm beyond nominal on the larger axis, up to five holes per land for the insert route, and up to eight holes per land for the doubler route. Beyond eight the land is replaced.
